steps.summary: Reused the persistent hero catalog, routed OP.GG pages through the shared client, persisted one normalized payload per canonical hero, restored stale payloads after restart, retained optional build data from the prior snapshot, and preserved canonical singleflight plus image caching.
Persist the existing bounded ban-query last-known-good cache across service restarts.
Return a final text/image/forward delivery envelope so GroupGuard does not parse business data.
Expose per-source live/cache/snapshot/stale/unavailable state, age, error class, and circuit state.
Add service, fixture, and pinned cross-repository contract tests including restart and no-public-network scenarios.
Deploy the backward-compatible service release before any GroupGuard runtime migration.

current_findings.summary: Shard and ARAM public source loading now use persistent infrastructure; ban-query last-known-good data remains memory-only until LAPI-BAN-001.
The currently deployed GroupGuard still downloads public shard and hero JSON directly until the later plugin migration.
The ARAM business path now uses the shared upstream client; the legacy helper remains only for compatibility tests and can be removed in a later cleanup after repository-wide reference review.
Current endpoints return business data or raw images but no uniform final delivery envelope for GroupGuard.

next_recommended_action.condition: Start only after LAPI-ARAM-001 passes Windows CI and endpoint compatibility review.
next_recommended_action.summary: Persist the bounded LOL ban last-known-good cache across service restarts without changing the current provider contract.

production_rule: The service release must remain compatible with the currently deployed GroupGuard, must be deployed first, and must pass restart plus upstream-failure acceptance before plugin migration.
